parsed.explanation: Thin-data jurisdiction; extrapolating from structural signals per the rubric. Worst documented features: (1) same-sex conduct de facto illegal, with 'good morals' provisions currently 'used against people' — an enforced morality lever, though its application to gender-nonconforming visitors is undocumented; (2) pervasive, current (2023) social and religious intolerance, taboo status, and fear of shunning — tier-3 societal hostility; (3) no SOGI discrimination protection, only an untested police/complaints channel; (4) hostile climate signals (LGBTI organisations cannot register, no public discussion tolerated, harsh-prison/opposition-suppression baseline). No documented universal-exposure measures, no documented police targeting or violence against trans people, no dated incidents — but the record is explicitly scarce, so that silence is not safety. No documented acceptance tradition to offset. This sits above jurisdictions with organised targeting or facility bans (0.25–0.35) but below those with documented acceptance plus working remedies (0.55+): latent-but-used morality law, thin recourse, and pervasive intolerance place it at the top of elevated risk.
